title: Superconducting ground state study of Cr-based equiatomic high-entropy alloy through $μ\text{SR}$
authors: Sonika Jangid, Rhea Stewart, Adrian D. Hillier, R. P. Singh
abstract: High-entropy alloy superconductors, characterized by extreme chemical disorder and complex electronic environments, have attracted significant attention as model systems for exploring superconductivity in disordered materials. Here, we investigate a Cr-based equiatomic HEA, Cr-V-Ti-Nb-Ta, which contains a magnetic 3d element, providing an opportunity to examine the influence of magnetic elements on superconductivity in highly disordered systems. Despite expected magnetic pair-breaking, this alloy exhibits bulk type-II superconductivity with a transition temperature of $T_c = 2.33(3)$ K and a high upper critical field. Transverse-field $μ$SR measurements reveal an s-wave superconducting gap close to the BCS value, while zero-field $μ$SR suggests preserved time-reversal symmetry. These results establish Cr-V-Ti-Nb-Ta as a promising platform for exploring the interplay between disorder, magnetism and superconductivity in high entropy alloys.
summary: This work reports on the superconducting properties of a disordered Cr-based High-Entropy Alloy (HEA). Using $\mu$SR and magnetic measurements, the authors confirm bulk superconductivity with an s-wave gap. The findings establish this HEA as a promising model system for understanding the complex interplay between chemical disorder, magnetism, and superconductivity.
main_problem: The study investigates how magnetic elements influence superconductivity within highly disordered High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs).
main_result: The Cr-V-Ti-Nb-Ta HEA exhibits bulk type-II superconductivity with a $T_c$ of 2.33 K, showing an s-wave gap and preserved time-reversal symmetry.
method: The research employed multiple experimental techniques including resistivity, magnetization (ZFCW/FCC), and Muon Spin Rotation ($\mu$SR) measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Cr-V-Ti-Nb-Ta equiatomic HEA, which crystallizes in a bcc structure and is characterized by significant chemical disorder.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), upper critical field ($H_{c2}$), superconducting gap symmetry (s-wave), and time-reversal symmetry preservation.
important_parameters: The material is analyzed in the context of disorder, magnetism, and the interplay between these factors in HEAs.
main_assumptions: The discrepancy between $T_c$ measured by resistivity and magnetization suggests potential superconducting inhomogeneity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate sample characterization (XRD, EDS, $ho(T)$) and superconducting properties, including magnetization hysteresis loops and field dependencies of $H_{c1}$ and $H_{c2}$.
paper_structure: The paper follows a standard experimental structure: characterization of the HEA, confirmation of bulk superconductivity via multiple measurements, detailed analysis of superconducting parameters using GL models, and finally, probing the pairing symmetry using $\mu$SR.
why_interesting: The combination of extreme disorder (HEA) and superconductivity provides a unique platform to test theories of unconventional pairing and pair-breaking mechanisms, which are relevant to understanding complex quantum many-body states.
